html:
The Charminar, "four towers", is a gateway and mosque built in 1591 at the centre of the new city of Hyderabad. It is the symbol of the city.

Its builder was Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, sultan of Golconda, one of the Deccan sultanates. His fortress of Golconda was crowded and short of water, so he laid out a new capital a few kilometres away across the Musi River. A legend says he built the Charminar to mark the end of a plague.

The building is a square, 20 metres on each side, with a great arch facing each direction. A minaret 56 metres high rises at each corner. A small mosque sits on the top floor. Four roads met under the arches and split the city into quarters. The chief minister, Mir Momin, an Iranian, planned the city on the model of Isfahan.

Golconda grew rich on diamonds from its mines, steel and printed cotton (see wootz steel). The sultan was also a poet, one of the first to write in Urdu.

Aurangzeb took Golconda in 1687. From 1724 the city was the capital of the Nizams (see Hyderabad State). The pearl and bangle markets still crowd around the monument.
sum: The Charminar, "four towers", is a gateway and mosque built in 1591 at the centre of the new city of Hyderabad. It is the symbol of the city.
